{"summary":"This narrow patch is safe and fixes the stated root cause. The only runtime change is the migration-name regex, which moves from `^\d{12,14}_` to `^(?:\d{8}|\d{12,14})_`. It now accepts 8-digit date-only folders, and 9–11-digit and 15+-digit prefixes are still rejected. Nothing changed in Docker isolation, loopback binding, tmpfs, marker-gated cleanup, env sanitization or receipt-shape logic. `verifyReceipt` uses the same updated list of migration names, so old 95-migration receipts are now correctly rejected as stale.

Ordering is consistent with Prisma. JS default `.sort()` and Prisma's directory sort both order ASCII names byte by byte. `_` (0x5F) sorts after digits, so `20261011_registration_form_retry_draft` runs after any `20261011xxxx` folder and before `20261012…`. The reported 96 migrations applying and 31/31 tests passing show this order works.

The new test is a two-way check. It fails if a folder with `migration.sql` is filtered out, and also if a folder matches the pattern but has no `migration.sql`. That directly guards against this class of failure. The hard-coded `20261011_…` check is an acceptable regression anchor.

One minor hardening point remains (below): the runner itself still drops non-matching folders silently and relies on the test to catch it.

Scope proposal (not a defect in this patch): `scripts/prisma-migrate-status-diagnostic.mjs` was not supplied. If it parses migration names with its own `\d{12,14}` pattern, 8-digit pending migrations could be misclassified in failure receipts. Worth a separate check.

An empty blocker/major list does not certify that tests or the release pass.","findings":[{"severity":"MINOR","file":"scripts/prisma-loopback-disposable-migration-runner.mjs","area":"listCanonicalMigrations (migrationNamePattern filter) and its use in main()/verifyReceipt","issue":"The runner still decides which migrations to run by matching names against an allowlist, and silently drops any folder that doesn't match. The new test catches this, but the runner itself doesn't stop. A future migration folder whose name doesn't match (for example 10 digits, a hyphen or uppercase letters) would again be skipped at runtime. `verifyReceipt` uses the same filter, so it would still accept the receipt as PASS.","evidence":"`.filter((entry) => entry.isDirectory() && migrationNamePattern.test(entry.name))` drops non-matching folders without any error. `main()` passes this list both to `writeMirror` and to `receipt.migrationNames`, and `verifyReceipt` compares against the same filtered list. This is the same failure that caused this incident (95 of 96 migrations applied, then a missing-table error).","impact":"If the runner is run without the test suite, or the test is skipped, the disposable database can again silently miss a migration. The runner would report PASS while the database lacks a production table, and later DB tests would fail with confusing missing-table errors.","recommended_fix":"Make `listCanonicalMigrations` stop with an error such as `migration-name-noncanonical` when a folder contains `migration.sql` but its name doesn't match the pattern. Keep the regex only as a guard against stray files, not as a way to choose which migrations run.","required_test":"Unit test: build a temporary migrations folder containing `2026101_bad/migration.sql` and pass it to `listCanonicalMigrations(directory)`. Assert that it throws. Keep the existing check that the list matches every source folder with `migration.sql`.","confidence":0.6}]}
